# Engage: The Mystery of Comet Borrelly

::: {.engage-box}
## ☄️ Frozen, Then Boiling — Every 6 Years

<div style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; margin: 20px 0; text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);">
Comet Borrelly has water that is frozen most of the time, but every several years it shoots out a jet of vaporized water and dust. Why?
</div>

The answer has everything to do with **orbits.** Borrelly's orbit takes it far from the Sun (where water freezes) and close to the Sun (where water vaporizes). The shape and size of its orbit determines where water can exist in each phase.

This is the same question we need to answer for exoplanets: **Does the planet's orbit keep it at the right temperature for liquid water throughout its entire year?**
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot = require("@observablehq/plot")
d3 = require("d3@7")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof borrellyTime = Inputs.range([0, 6.85], {label: "Time (years):", step: 0.05, value: 0})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const t = borrellyTime;
  const solveE = (M, e) => { let E = M; for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) E = E - (E - e * Math.sin(E) - M) / (1 - e * Math.cos(E)); return E; };

  const W = 360, H = 365;
  const sx = 175, sy = 170, scale = 24;

  const aE = 1.0, eE = 0.017;
  const ME = 2 * Math.PI * (t % 1.0), EE = solveE(ME, eE);
  const aB = 3.61, eB = 0.62, cB = aB * eB, bB = aB * Math.sqrt(1 - eB*eB);
  const MB = 2 * Math.PI * (t / 6.85), EB = solveE(MB, eB);

  const cxE = sx - aE * eE * scale, cyE = sy;
  const cxB = sx - cB * scale, cyB = sy;
  const ex = cxE + aE * scale * Math.cos(EE), ey = cyE + aE * scale * Math.sin(EE);
  const bx = cxB + aB * scale * Math.cos(EB), by = cyB + bB * scale * Math.sin(EB);
  const rE = aE * (1 - eE * Math.cos(EE));
  const rB = aB * (1 - eB * Math.cos(EB));
  const state = rB < 1.6 ? "💧 near the Sun — ice vaporizes" : rB > 2.5 ? "❄️ far from the Sun — frozen" : "🌡️ warming up";
  const stateColor = rB < 1.6 ? "#f39c12" : rB > 2.5 ? "#74b9ff" : "#f6e05e";

  const svg = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto")
    .style("max-width", "520px").style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("fill", "#0a0a2e").attr("rx", 12);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 20).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "white").attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text("Comet Borrelly vs. Earth");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 38).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "#9aa7bd").attr("font-size", 10)
    .text("🟢 Earth (period 1 yr)   ·   🟣 Borrelly (period 6.85 yr)");

  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cxE).attr("cy", cyE).attr("r", aE * scale)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#2ecc71").attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
  svg.append("ellipse").attr("cx", cxB).attr("cy", cyB).attr("rx", aB * scale).attr("ry", bB * scale)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#a29bfe").attr("stroke-width", 1.5);

  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", sx).attr("cy", sy).attr("r", 7).attr("fill", "#f39c12");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", sx).attr("y", sy + 18).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "#f39c12").attr("font-size", 9).attr("font-weight", "bold").text("Sun");

  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", ex).attr("cy", ey).attr("r", 5).attr("fill", "#2ecc71").attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 1);
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", bx).attr("cy", by).attr("r", 5).attr("fill", stateColor).attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 1);

  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 315).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "#2ecc71").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text(`Earth: ${rE.toFixed(2)} AU (nearly constant)`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 338).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", stateColor).attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text(`Borrelly: ${rB.toFixed(2)} AU — ${state}`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 358).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "#9aa7bd").attr("font-size", 8)
    .text("Orbits are to scale; bodies are not. Drag the slider to walk through 6.85 years.");

  return svg.node();
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45);
      transition:transform .15s,box-shadow .15s;"
      onmouseover="this.style.transform='scale(1.04)';this.style.boxShadow='0 5px 18px rgba(102,126,234,.55)'"
      onmouseout="this.style.transform='scale(1)';this.style.boxShadow='0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45)'"
    >
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="2000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

# Explore 1: Patterns in Solar System Data

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔬 Kepler's Third Law — The Mathematical Pattern

When you graph orbital period vs. distance from the Sun for all planets, an elegant pattern emerges.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
solarSystem = [
  {name: "Mercury", period: 0.241, distance: 0.387, type: "Rocky planet"},
  {name: "Venus", period: 0.615, distance: 0.723, type: "Rocky planet"},
  {name: "Earth", period: 1.0, distance: 1.0, type: "Rocky planet"},
  {name: "Mars", period: 1.881, distance: 1.524, type: "Rocky planet"},
  {name: "Jupiter", period: 11.86, distance: 5.203, type: "Gas giant"},
  {name: "Saturn", period: 29.46, distance: 9.537, type: "Gas giant"},
  {name: "Uranus", period: 84.01, distance: 19.19, type: "Ice giant"},
  {name: "Neptune", period: 164.8, distance: 30.07, type: "Ice giant"},
  {name: "Comet Borrelly", period: 6.85, distance: 3.61, type: "Comet"}
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof keplerScale = Inputs.radio(["Log scale", "Linear scale"], {label: "Axes:", value: "Log scale"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const log = keplerScale === "Log scale";
  const fmt = d => d >= 1 ? String(d) : String(+d.toFixed(2));
  const typeColors = {
    domain: ["Rocky planet", "Gas giant", "Ice giant", "Comet"],

  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    title: "Kepler's Third Law: Period² ∝ Distance³",
    subtitle: log ? "Log axes turn the power law into a straight line" : "Linear axes — watch the inner planets cram into the corner",
    width: width,
    height: 400,
    marginLeft: 48,
    marginRight: 10,
    marginBottom: 40,
    color: { domain: typeColors.domain, range: typeColors.range },
    x: {label: "Average Distance from Sun (AU)", type: log ? "log" : "linear", grid: true, tickFormat: fmt},
    y: {label: "Orbital Period (years)", type: log ? "log" : "linear", grid: true, tickFormat: fmt},
    marks: [
      Plot.dot(solarSystem, {
        x: "distance",
        y: "period",
        fill: "type",
        r: 7,
        stroke: "#333",
        strokeWidth: 0.5,
        title: d => `${d.name}\nDistance: ${d.distance} AU\nPeriod: ${d.period} yr`,
        tip: true
      }),
      ...(log ? [Plot.text(solarSystem, {
        x: "distance",
        y: "period",
        text: "name",
        dx: 10,
        dy: -6,
        fontSize: 10,
        fontWeight: "bold"
      })] : []),
      Plot.line(
        d3.range(0.2, 35, 0.1).map(d => ({x: d, y: Math.pow(d, 1.5)})),
        {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#667eea", strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "5,5"}
      )
    ]
  }));
  wrap.append("div")
    .style("display", "flex").style("flex-wrap", "wrap")
    .style("gap", "6px 16px").style("justify-content", "center")
    .style("margin-top", "10px").style("font-size", "0.85em")
    .html(typeColors.domain.map((s, i) =>
      `<span style="display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;">` +
      `<span style="width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:${typeColors.range[i]};border:1px solid #333;flex:0 0 auto;"></span>` +
      `${s}</span>`).join(""));
  return wrap.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Kepler's Third Law

$$T^2 = a^3$$

Where:

- $T$ = orbital period (in years)
- $a$ = semi-major axis / average distance (in AU)

This means: **if you know how long a planet takes to orbit its star, you can calculate its distance.** This is exactly how we figure out exoplanet orbits — we measure the period and calculate the distance!
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildQuiz("kepler-law-quiz", "📌 Check Your Understanding — Kepler's Third Law", [
  {
    q: "Mars has an orbital period of 1.881 years and a distance of 1.524 AU. Does Kepler's Third Law (T² = a³) hold? Calculate T² and a³.",
    options: ["T² = 3.54, a³ = 3.54 — Yes, they match!", "T² = 1.88, a³ = 1.52 — No, they don't match", "T² = 3.54, a³ = 4.57 — Close but not exact", "T² = 2.0, a³ = 2.0 — Only works for Earth"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "T² = 1.881² = 3.538 and a³ = 1.524³ = 3.540. They match almost perfectly! This elegant relationship holds for every object orbiting the Sun."
  },
  {
    q: "Comet Borrelly has an orbital period of 6.85 years. Using T² = a³, what is its average distance from the Sun?",
    options: ["About 2.3 AU", "About 3.6 AU", "About 6.85 AU", "About 46.9 AU"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "T² = 6.85² = 46.9. Then a = ³√46.9 ≈ 3.6 AU. Kepler's Third Law lets us calculate distance from period alone — essential for analyzing exoplanets we can't directly observe."
  },
  {
    q: "Why is Kepler's Third Law especially useful for studying exoplanets?",
    options: ["It tells us the planet's mass", "It lets us calculate orbital distance from the period, which we can measure via transit timing", "It determines the planet's atmospheric composition", "It predicts whether the planet has moons"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "For exoplanets, we can measure the orbital period by timing how often the planet transits (crosses in front of) its star. Kepler's Third Law then gives us the distance — and distance determines whether the planet is in the habitable zone."
  }
])
```

# Explain 1: The Habitable Zone

::: {.explain-box}
## 🧠 The "Goldilocks Zone" — Not Too Hot, Not Too Cold

A planet needs to be at just the right distance from its star for liquid water to exist. Too close → water boils. Too far → water freezes. This narrow band is the **habitable zone.**
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof starLum = Inputs.range([0.01, 10], {label: "Star luminosity (× Sun):", step: 0.01, value: 1.0})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
exoplanets = [
  {name: "Kepler-442b", period: 112.3, distance: 0.409, ecc: 0.04, starLum: 0.12, zone: "In HZ"},
  {name: "Kepler-186f", period: 129.9, distance: 0.432, ecc: 0.04, starLum: 0.04, zone: "In HZ"},
  {name: "TRAPPIST-1e", period: 6.1, distance: 0.029, ecc: 0.005, starLum: 0.0005, zone: "In HZ"},
  {name: "Kepler-22b", period: 289.9, distance: 0.849, ecc: 0.0, starLum: 0.79, zone: "In HZ"},
  {name: "Kepler-452b", period: 384.8, distance: 1.046, ecc: 0.035, starLum: 1.2, zone: "In HZ"},
  {name: "55 Cancri e", period: 0.74, distance: 0.015, ecc: 0.17, starLum: 0.6, zone: "Too hot"},
  {name: "Kepler-16b", period: 228.8, distance: 0.704, ecc: 0.007, starLum: 0.15, zone: "Too cold"}
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const inner = L => Math.sqrt(L / 1.1);
  const outer = L => Math.sqrt(L / 0.53);
  const fmt = d => d >= 1 ? String(d) : String(+d.toFixed(2));
  const Ls = d3.range(0.01, 10.01, 0.01);
  const hzBand = Ls.map(L => ({ L, inner: inner(L), outer: outer(L) }));

  const solar = [
    {name: "Venus", lum: 1, dist: 0.72},
    {name: "Earth", lum: 1, dist: 1.0},
    {name: "Mars", lum: 1, dist: 1.52}
  ];
  const points = [
    ...solar.map(d => ({...d, kind: "planet"})),
    ...exoplanets.map(d => ({name: d.name, lum: d.starLum, dist: d.distance, kind: "exo"}))
  ].map(d => ({
    ...d,
    zone: d.dist < inner(d.lum) ? "Too hot" : d.dist > outer(d.lum) ? "Too cold" : "In HZ"
  }));

  const zoneColors = {
    domain: ["In HZ", "Too hot", "Too cold"],
    range: ["#2ecc71", "#e74c3c", "#3498db"]
  };

  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.style("max-width", "100%");
  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    title: "The Habitable Zone",
    subtitle: `Star luminosity ${starLum.toFixed(2)}× Sun → habitable zone ${inner(starLum).toFixed(2)}–${outer(starLum).toFixed(2)} AU`,
    width: width,
    height: 420,
    marginLeft: 46,
    marginRight: 10,
    marginBottom: 40,
    style: { background: "#0a0a2e", color: "#e2e8f0", fontFamily: "sans-serif" },
    color: { domain: zoneColors.domain, range: zoneColors.range },
    x: {label: "Star luminosity (× Sun)", type: "log", domain: [0.01, 10], grid: true, tickFormat: fmt},
    y: {label: "Orbital distance (AU)", type: "log", grid: true, tickFormat: fmt},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(hzBand, {x: "L", y1: "inner", y2: "outer", fill: "#2ecc71", opacity: 0.15}),
      Plot.dot(points, {
        x: "lum", y: "dist", fill: "zone",
        r: 6, stroke: "#0a0a2e", strokeWidth: 1,
        title: d => `${d.name}\nStar luminosity: ${d.lum}× Sun\nDistance: ${d.dist} AU\n${d.zone}`,
        tip: true
      }),
      Plot.text(points.filter(d => d.kind === "planet"), {
        x: "lum", y: "dist", text: "name", dx: 10, dy: -4, fontSize: 11, fontWeight: "bold", fill: "#e2e8f0"
      }),
      Plot.ruleX([starLum], {stroke: "#ffffff", strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "4,4", strokeOpacity: 0.7})
    ]
  }));
  wrap.append("div")
    .style("display", "flex").style("flex-wrap", "wrap")
    .style("gap", "6px 16px").style("justify-content", "center")
    .style("margin-top", "10px").style("font-size", "0.85em").style("color", "#e2e8f0")
    .html(zoneColors.domain.map((s, i) =>
      `<span style="display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;">` +
      `<span style="width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:${zoneColors.range[i]};border:1px solid #e2e8f0;flex:0 0 auto;"></span>` +
      `${s}</span>`).join(""));
  return wrap.node();
}
```

# Explore 2: Orbital Eccentricity

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔬 Not All Orbits Are Circles

Real orbits are **ellipses** — some nearly circular, others very elongated. The **eccentricity** ($e$) measures how stretched an orbit is:
- $e = 0$: perfect circle
- $e = 0.5$: moderately elliptical
- $e = 1$: parabola (escape trajectory)
- **Kepler's Second Law:** a planet moves fastest at perihelion (closest) and slowest at aphelion — watch the speed and ☀️ energy readouts in the animation below.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof eccentricity = Inputs.range([0, 0.9], {label: "Orbital eccentricity:", step: 0.01, value: 0.017})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof semiMajor = Inputs.range([0.5, 3.0], {label: "Semi-major axis (AU):", step: 0.1, value: 1.0})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const a = semiMajor;
  const e = eccentricity;
  const b = a * Math.sqrt(1 - e * e);
  const c = a * e;
  const perihelion = a * (1 - e);
  const aphelion = a * (1 + e);

  const inHZ = perihelion >= 0.95 * 0.95 && aphelion <= 1.37 * 1.05;
  const partialHZ = perihelion < 1.37 && aphelion > 0.95;

  // Logical viewBox scales responsively via CSS (mobile-first)
  const W = 360, H = 400, ox = 180, oy = 200;
  const m = 42, top = 58, bottom = 338;

  // Fit both the orbit and the 0.95–1.37 AU habitable-zone ring inside the box
  const scaleF = Math.min(
    100,
    (ox - m) / Math.max(a * (1 + e), 1.37),
    (W - ox - m) / Math.max(a * (1 - e), 1.37),
    (oy - top) / Math.max(b, 1.37),
    (bottom - oy) / Math.max(b, 1.37)
  );

  const cx = ox - c * scaleF;  // ellipse center (empty focus sits left of the Sun)
  const svg = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto")
    .style("max-width", "520px").style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("fill", "#0a0a2e").attr("rx", 12);

  // Habitable zone: translucent annulus + dashed boundary circles
  const annulus = d3.path();
  annulus.arc(ox, oy, 1.37 * scaleF, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
  annulus.arc(ox, oy, 0.95 * scaleF, 0, 2 * Math.PI, true);
  svg.append("path").attr("d", annulus).attr("fill-rule", "evenodd")
    .attr("fill", "#2ecc71").attr("opacity", 0.10);
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", ox).attr("cy", oy).attr("r", 1.37 * scaleF)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#2ecc71").attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", ox).attr("cy", oy).attr("r", 0.95 * scaleF)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#2ecc71").attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");

  // Orbit ellipse
  const orbitColor = inHZ ? "#2ecc71" : partialHZ ? "#f39c12" : "#e74c3c";
  svg.append("ellipse")
    .attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", oy)
    .attr("rx", a * scaleF).attr("ry", b * scaleF)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", orbitColor).attr("stroke-width", 2);

  // Sun at focus + perihelion/aphelion markers
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", ox).attr("cy", oy).attr("r", 7).attr("fill", "#f39c12");
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx + a * scaleF).attr("cy", oy).attr("r", 4).attr("fill", "#e74c3c");
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx - a * scaleF).attr("cy", oy).attr("r", 4).attr("fill", "#3498db");

  // Header
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 22).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "white").attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text(`Eccentricity: ${e.toFixed(2)} | Semi-major axis: ${a.toFixed(1)} AU`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", 40).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "#ccc").attr("font-size", 11)
    .text(`Perihelion ${perihelion.toFixed(2)} AU · Aphelion ${aphelion.toFixed(2)} AU`);

  // Status
  const status = inHZ ? "✅ Stays within habitable zone all year!" :
                 partialHZ ? "⚠️ Partially in habitable zone — water may freeze/boil seasonally" :
                 "❌ Outside habitable zone";
  const statusColor = inHZ ? "#2ecc71" : partialHZ ? "#f39c12" : "#e74c3c";
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", bottom + 18).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", statusColor).attr("font-size", 13).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text(status);

  // Legend
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W/2).attr("y", H - 6).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("fill", "#2ecc71").attr("font-size", 10)
    .text("Green = habitable zone (0.95–1.37 AU for a Sun-like star)");

  // Animated planet: radial line + dot + live readout
  const line = svg.append("line").attr("x1", ox).attr("y1", oy).attr("x2", ox).attr("y2", oy)
    .attr("stroke", "rgba(253,224,71,0.8)").attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
  const planet = svg.append("circle").attr("r", 6).attr("fill", "#4ade80").attr("stroke", "#bbf7d0").attr("stroke-width", 1);
  const live = svg.append("text").attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("fill", "#fef3c7").attr("font-size", 10);

  let E = 0;
  let raf = 0;
  let last = performance.now();
  const K = 1.05;  // angular rate (rad/s) at r = 1 AU; speeds up near perihelion
  function step(ts) {
    const dt = Math.min((ts - last) / 1000, 0.05);
    last = ts;
    const r = a * (1 - e * Math.cos(E));
    E += (dt * K) / r;
    if (E >= Math.PI * 2) E -= Math.PI * 2;
    const px = cx + a * scaleF * Math.cos(E);
    const py = oy + b * scaleF * Math.sin(E);
    planet.attr("cx", px).attr("cy", py);
    line.attr("x2", px).attr("y2", py);
    live.attr("x", px).attr("y", py - 10)
      .attr("text-anchor", px < W / 2 ? "start" : "end")
      .text(`${r.toFixed(2)} AU · ${(a / r).toFixed(2)}× speed · ☀️ ${((a / r) ** 2).toFixed(1)}× energy`);
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  }
  raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  invalidation.then(() => cancelAnimationFrame(raf));

  return svg.node();
}
```

# Elaborate: Applying to Exoplanets

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🌍 Real Exoplanet Data

Scientists have discovered thousands of exoplanets using the Kepler Space Telescope. For each one, we can measure the orbital period — and use Kepler's Third Law to calculate the orbit.
:::

# Chapter Summary

| Key Concept | Details |
|---|---|
| **Kepler's Third Law** | $T^2 = a^3$ — period and distance are mathematically linked |
| **Habitable Zone** | Region where liquid water can exist; HZ = $\sqrt{L/1.1}$ to $\sqrt{L/0.53}$ AU |
| **Eccentricity** | Measures orbit shape (0 = circle, ~1 = very elongated); must be low for habitability |
| **Earth's orbit** | $a = 1.0$ AU, $e = 0.017$ (nearly circular), stays in HZ year-round |
| **Comet Borrelly** | $e = 0.62$ — orbit explains water phase changes (frozen ↔ vaporized) |
| **Exoplanet analysis** | Measure period → calculate distance → check if in HZ with low eccentricity |

# Myth or Fact?

```{=html}
<div id="orbit-myths" style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1a1a2e 0%,#16213e 50%,#0f3460 100%); color:white; padding:30px; border-radius:16px; margin:30px 0; font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; box-shadow:0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);">
  <h2 style="font-family:'Space Grotesk',sans-serif; font-size:1.8em; margin:0 0 8px 0; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#3498db,#2ecc71); -webkit-background-clip:text; -webkit-text-fill-color:transparent;">
    🪐 Planets & Orbits: Myths vs. Facts

  </div>
  <div id="omf-card" style="background:rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius:14px; padding:28px; min-height:100px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; text-align:center; font-size:1.1em; font-weight:600; line-height:1.6; border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);"></div>

    <button id="omf-myth" onclick="omfAnswer('Myth')" style="flex:1; padding:14px; border:none; border-radius:10px; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#e17055,#d63031); color:white; font-size:1em; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 4px 15px rgba(214,48,49,0.3);">❌ MYTH</button>
    <button id="omf-fact" onclick="omfAnswer('Fact')" style="flex:1; padding:14px; border:none; border-radius:10px; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#00b894,#00cec9); color:white; font-size:1em; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 4px 15px rgba(0,184,148,0.3);">✅ FACT</button>

  <button id="omf-next" onclick="omfNext()" style="display:none; margin-top:12px; width:100%; padding:12px; border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.2); border-radius:10px; background:transparent; color:white; font-size:0.95em; font-weight:600; cursor:pointer;">Next Card →</button>

    <button onclick="omfRestart()" style="margin-top:12px; padding:10px 24px; border:2px solid #3498db; border-radius:20px; background:transparent; color:#3498db; font-size:0.9em; cursor:pointer; font-weight:600;">Play Again</button>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function() {
  var cards = [
    {
      text: "Planets orbit the Sun in perfect circles.",
      type: "Myth",
      explanation: "All planetary orbits are ellipses, not circles. Earth's orbit is nearly circular (e = 0.017), but many objects have noticeably elliptical orbits. Kepler discovered this in the 1600s, overturning the ancient Greek idea of perfect circular motion."
    },
    {
      text: "Earth is closest to the Sun during Northern Hemisphere summer.",
      type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Earth is actually closest to the Sun (perihelion) in January — during Northern Hemisphere winter! Seasons are caused by Earth's 23.5° axial tilt, not by distance from the Sun. The distance varies by only ~3% due to our low eccentricity."
    },
    {
      text: "Kepler's Third Law (T² = a³) applies to any object orbiting any star, not just our Sun.",
      type: "Fact",
      explanation: "The generalized form is T² = (4π²/GM)a³, which works for any star mass M. When using solar masses and AU/years, it simplifies to T² = a³/M. This is exactly how astronomers determine exoplanet distances from observed orbital periods."
    },
    {
      text: "A planet with an eccentricity of 0.5 would experience dramatic temperature swings during its orbit.",
      type: "Fact",
      explanation: "With e = 0.5, the planet's closest approach is half its average distance, and its farthest point is 1.5× its average distance. Since stellar radiation follows an inverse-square law, the planet receives 9× more energy at perihelion than at aphelion — extreme seasonal swings."
    },
    {
      text: "The habitable zone is the same distance from every star.",
      type: "Myth",
      explanation: "The habitable zone depends on stellar luminosity. Dim M-type stars have habitable zones at 0.1–0.2 AU; bright stars push the HZ out to 2–3+ AU. The formula HZ = √(L/threshold) shows the direct dependence on luminosity."
    },
    {
      text: "Scientists can determine an exoplanet's orbital distance by measuring how frequently it passes in front of its star.",
      type: "Fact",
      explanation: "The transit method measures the orbital period (time between transits). Kepler's Third Law then converts period to distance: a = (T²)^(1/3). This technique has been used to characterize thousands of exoplanets discovered by the Kepler and TESS missions."
    },
    {
      text: "Comet Borrelly's water changes between ice and vapor because the comet generates internal heat.",
      type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Comets don't generate heat. Borrelly's highly elliptical orbit (e = 0.62) carries it from ~5.85 AU (far, cold) to ~1.37 AU (close, warm). Near the Sun, solar radiation vaporizes surface ice into jets. Far away, temperatures drop and water freezes solid again."
    },
    {
      text: "For an exoplanet to support life, it needs both the right orbital distance AND a low eccentricity to stay in the habitable zone year-round.",
      type: "Fact",
      explanation: "A planet at the right average distance but with high eccentricity will swing in and out of the habitable zone. Water would alternately boil and freeze each 'year.' Low eccentricity (< ~0.2) ensures the planet receives consistent energy for stable liquid water."
    }
  ];
  var idx = 0, score = 0, answered = 0, cardAnswered = false;
  function updateCard() {
    if (idx >= cards.length) {
      document.getElementById('omf-card').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('omf-myth').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('omf-fact').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('omf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('omf-next').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('omf-done').style.display = 'block';
      document.getElementById('omf-final').textContent = score;
      return;
    }
    document.getElementById('omf-card').textContent = cards[idx].text;
    document.getElementById('omf-progress').textContent = 'Card ' + (idx + 1) + ' of ' + cards.length;
    document.getElementById('omf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
    document.getElementById('omf-next').style.display = 'none';
    document.getElementById('omf-myth').disabled = false;
    document.getElementById('omf-fact').disabled = false;
    document.getElementById('omf-myth').style.opacity = '1';
    document.getElementById('omf-fact').style.opacity = '1';
    cardAnswered = false;
  }
  window.omfAnswer = function(choice) {
    if (cardAnswered) return;
    cardAnswered = true;
    answered++;
    var card = cards[idx];
    var correct = (choice === card.type);
    if (correct) score++;
    document.getElementById('omf-score').textContent = score;
    document.getElementById('omf-total').textContent = answered;
    var fb = document.getElementById('omf-feedback');
    fb.style.display = 'block';
    fb.style.background = correct ? 'rgba(0,184,148,0.2)' : 'rgba(214,48,49,0.2)';
    fb.style.border = '1px solid ' + (correct ? '#00b894' : '#e17055');
    fb.innerHTML = '<strong>' + (correct ? '✅ Correct! ' : '❌ That\'s a ' + card.type + '! ') + '</strong>' + card.explanation;
    document.getElementById('omf-myth').disabled = true;
    document.getElementById('omf-fact').disabled = true;
    document.getElementById('omf-myth').style.opacity = (choice === 'Myth') ? '1' : '0.5';
    document.getElementById('omf-fact').style.opacity = (choice === 'Fact') ? '1' : '0.5';
    document.getElementById('omf-next').style.display = 'block';
  };
  window.omfNext = function() { idx++; updateCard(); };
  window.omfRestart = function() {
    idx = 0; score = 0; answered = 0;
    document.getElementById('omf-card').style.display = 'flex';
    document.getElementById('omf-myth').style.display = 'block';
    document.getElementById('omf-fact').style.display = 'block';
    document.getElementById('omf-done').style.display = 'none';
    document.getElementById('omf-score').textContent = '0';
    document.getElementById('omf-total').textContent = '0';
    updateCard();
  };
  updateCard();
})();
</script>
```

# End-of-Chapter Quiz

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildOrbitQuiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.85;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #c7d2fe;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f8f9ff;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null;
          b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";btn.style.color="#276749";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
          correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";fb.style.borderRadius="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```
